prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin street corner from
the same camera position, the same vertical framing, the same deserted
pavement, the same pedestrian traffic light on its grey pole with the upper
round lens glowing an even plain red, the same pale cream facade with its
stone-framed windows, the same black city bicycles along the wall, the same
granite kerb, the same flat overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is the markings painted on the road at the bottom of the
picture: the pedestrian crossing starts at the foot of the traffic light,
and the red bicycle strip holds ONE EVEN WIDTH along its whole length and
TURNS.

The pedestrian crossing begins on the asphalt at the granite kerb, at the
foot of the grey pole that carries the traffic light, and runs from there
toward the bottom edge of the picture: broad white bars, the same bars as
in the second reference photograph, each bar as wide as the strip of grey
asphalt beside it.

The red bicycle strip lies to the LEFT of the crossing, its right-hand edge
against the first white bar. Coming up from the bottom edge of the picture
it runs straight toward the kerb, as wide as a bicycle lane; at the kerb it
bends to the LEFT and runs along the road on the road side of the granite
kerb, leaving the picture at its left edge, still exactly as wide there as
at the bend. It is one continuous ribbon of red asphalt with a dashed white
line along each of its two edges, and one white bicycle pictogram painted
flat on it below the bend.
